items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: The one you're referring to I think is the one that was with Fletcher Henderson.

ctx.x: Well I know Buster quite well.

Now there is two Buster Bailey's. The one you're referring to I think is the one that was with Fletcher Henderson. Yeah. Well there is another one that was from Dallas that went to Europe and never came back. Well I don't know. Did he play Clarence also? Yes he was terrific. Really?
I didn't know that. Two of them.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: he'd feature Buster Bailey on Memphis Blue.

ctx.x: So for instance, there never was one individual that stood out and the whole number built around him. It was a band. And it featured everyone in the band that could play.

But you go to, you used to go to Louis Armstrong concerts, say in the 50s and the 60s. And he would then, he'd have one number, like he'd have a program built in such a way that he'd feature Buster Bailey on Memphis Blue. But that was a later thing. You never had a star deal.

Yeah, but here's the difference here. There was only five or six pieces there. Mine, I had 14. So you couldn't combine it to one individual. But five piece bands, yes, that's how they had to operate. Well, for instance, the concert last night, it would have been lost if you couldn't feature each individual.
